gotcha.title: Putting the request body first
gotcha.looks_fine: When the request reaches your code as one object, you can read the body at any point in the function. Here the order of the arguments is the order in which the parts are extracted.
gotcha.rust_sees: In axum the handler's arguments are the extractors, and they run from left to right. The docs say the request body is "an asynchronous stream that can only be consumed once", so axum requires an extractor that consumes it (`Json`, `String`, `Bytes`) to be the last argument.
gotcha.why: The error is long because axum works this out through traits: a function whose arguments are in the wrong order no longer counts as a handler. When you see "the trait `Handler<_, _>` is not implemented", check the argument order first. With axum's `macros` feature, `#[axum::debug_handler]` above the function puts a short message first: "`Json<_>` consumes the request body and thus must be the last argument to the handler function" (the long error still follows it in the run above).

fixed.name: src/main.rs

go.says: In Go you choose where in the handler to read the body, once, with `json.NewDecoder(r.Body)`, as this page's Go service does.
